checks.method: Read TwoStarResidual.lean and reconstructed the outside-point contradiction in Section 3.1, allowing residual points anywhere in the ambient type.
checks.observation: If R has at least two points outside U, every y-star member has the additional outside point y. A member disjoint from R would give at least three distinct outside points in an eight-point union whose transversal restriction to U needs six points. Hence every y-link triple meets R, contradicting transversal number six because |R|=4. The argument uses the actual stars and no assumed coverage of the ambient support.
checks.scope: Two-star residual trace under unrestricted ambient support

checks.method: Read CompletionCompatibility.lean and checked the empty, singleton and two-point intersections of two A-coordinate edges when their B-coordinate edges are disjoint.
checks.observation: Empty intersection makes two completions and the original row a disjoint triple; equal A-edges permit the original a-extended design block as a third member; singleton intersection q permits a design block through q avoiding the other two endpoints, since at most four of five blocks are forbidden. Each constructed third member is distinct because it contains x. Coordinatewise intersection then limits each cycle projection to two edges and yields at most four distinct unions.

checks.method: Checked the total-weight contradiction analytically and independently enumerated all six-coordinate nonnegative integer weight vectors of total at most ten in Python; retained scratch/chief/round03_weight_check.json.
checks.observation: A heavy pair of weight at least nine has a point of weight at least five. Any heavy pair omitting it would force total weight at least fourteen, impossible. Exhaustive diagnostic examined 8008 vectors, including 687 with a heavy pair, and found no counterexample even when all heavy pairs are admitted. The actual proof requires only this elementary argument and injectivity of Q↦Q∪{a}; it does not require injectivity of Q↦E(Q). The diagnostic is corroboration, not a new formal premise.

checks.method: Read MinimumTransversals.lean and compared its prescribed-component hypotheses and conclusion with the revised Section 1 paragraph.
checks.observation: The helper restricts a six-point transversal to the two disjoint supports. Each restriction needs at least three points, so both have exactly three and their union exhausts the transversal; inherited component classification makes each restriction a design block. The current manuscript attributes this synchronization to the new Frontier helper while retaining the component ingredients as inherited.
checks.scope: Synchronized minimum-transversal claim and attribution repair

content.summary: The structural proof chain survives targeted rival-case checks. Arbitrary points outside the two link supports cannot evade the residual trace argument; all three possible intersection sizes of completion-coordinate edges are covered; and common-extension concentration does not require an unproved extension-pair permutation. The revised attribution correctly distinguishes the new synchronized transversal helper from its inherited component facts. No counterexample or required revision arose in this phase.
